title: The Cost of Breaking Convention
heading: Optional Guideline: The Cost of Breaking Convention
summary: Optional guideline that penalizes a magus who dresses above his station, trails armed men, or flaunts his familiar in public when dealing with mundanes, unless he makes an effort to follow convention.
quotes: he suffers an additional –1 social interaction penalty

title: The Process in Brief (Fourth Estate)
heading: The Process in Brief
requires: Saga arc: Order of Hermes as the Fourth Estate
summary: Outlines the sequence of steps a covenant follows to move the Order toward integration with mundane society, from test cases at Tribunal through negotiation with nobles and Church to the Grand Tribunal.

title: A Life's Work (pacing the Fourth Estate)
heading: A Life's Work
requires: Saga arc: Order of Hermes as the Fourth Estate
summary: Suggests measuring the pace of the integration saga in Tribunal meetings, with a fair-pace schedule of what happens at each successive Tribunal.
quotes: With Tribunals held every seven years and a Grand Tribunal every 33 years

title: Preparing for Tribunal Debate
heading: The Tribunal
requires: Saga arc: Order of Hermes as the Fourth Estate
summary: Explains that the final integration debate is run with the Tribunal debate rules from Houses of Hermes: Societates, and that an argument bonus earned earlier from polemic texts can be applied to it.
quotes: it can be applied to any debate which encompasses aspects of the polemic philosophy

title: Mundane Testimony at Tribunal
heading: Mundane Testimony
requires: Saga arc: Order of Hermes as the Fourth Estate
summary: Mundanes may attend Tribunal and give testimony in support of or against a case; mechanically this gives a small bonus to argument strength, with most of the value being roleplaying.
quotes: the testimony adds +1 to the argument strength

title: A New Breed of Craftsman (Rego Craft Magic and Finesse)
heading: A New Breed of Craftsman
summary: Explains that Rego Craft Magic items rely on the user's Finesse for quality and are harder than mundane craftsmanship, so specialists skilled in Finesse become valuable as magical tools spread.
quotes: the quality of the produced item is dependent on a Finesse roll against an Ease Factor that is always at least 3 points higher than that needed by a mundane craftsman

title: Writing and Responding to Polemic
heading: Writing and Responding to Polemic
summary: Introduces the activity of writing persuasive texts in advance of a Tribunal debate, using three forms of writing: polemic, diatribe and apologia.

title: Polemic
heading: Polemic
summary: A polemic is a summa or tractatus on a knowledge Ability such as Code of Hermes or Order of Hermes Lore that argues for a philosophical position; for these rules a polemic tractatus counts as Level 5.
quotes: tractatus have a Level of 5

title: Diatribe
heading: Diatribe
summary: A diatribe is a critical text written on the same Ability as the polemic it attacks, intended to damage the position and its proponents; each tractatus counts against the author's normal tractatus limit.
quotes: Each tractatus counts towards the normal limit on the number of tractatus that the author may write.

title: Apologia
heading: Apologia
summary: An apologia is a defensive rebuttal written on the same Ability as the diatribe it answers, strengthening the original proposition; each tractatus counts against the author's normal limit.
quotes: Each tractatus counts towards the normal limit on the number of tractatus that the author may write.

title: Like Father, Like Son (Views from Polemic)
heading: Like Father, Like Son
summary: A character who gains their first level in a knowledge Ability by reading a polemic is assumed to share the author's views on that subject.
quotes: any character gaining his first level in a knowledge Ability through reading polemic shares the author's views on that subject

title: The Prevailing Wisdom
heading: The Prevailing Wisdom
summary: The base difficulty of altering opinion in writing depends on how broad the change is; the level is read from the Prevailing Wisdom table.

title: Prevailing Wisdom Table
heading: Prevailing Wisdom Table
summary: Table giving the base level of the prevailing wisdom according to whether the change concerns a magus, covenant, Tribunal, House or the whole Order.
quotes: The higher of 3 or the magus' reputation

title: Prevailing Wisdom Examples
heading: Prevailing Wisdom Examples
summary: Table of sample topics with the Ease Factor that applies to changing opinion about them, and the reason for each.

title: Winning the Argument
heading: Winning the Argument
summary: Describes how a polemic is written and why it must be of a level high enough to entice readers; its Quality contributes to a bonus in debate at Tribunal.
quotes: Polemical tractatus are treated as level 5 for the purposes of circulating them.
related: Houses of Hermes: Societates p.91 Debate

title: Circulating the Text
heading: Circulating the Text
summary: A polemic must be circulated through copies, with a seasonal Circulation Roll against an Ease Factor set by the audience; success grants the author a Supporter of (ideal) Reputation.
quotes: Circulation Total: Magus' Reputation + Summa Level (or 5 in the case of tractatus) + Simple Die
Ease Factor: 15 (Tribunal), 18 (House), 24 (the Order)
Each season spent circulating a text provides a bonus of +1 to the next Circulation Total.

title: The Argument Total
heading: The Argument Total
summary: Once circulated, the author works out an Argument Total from text quality minus the prevailing wisdom level, which converts into a debate bonus or penalty at Tribunal.
quotes: Argument Total: Text Quality – Prevailing Wisdom Level
the final Argument Total acts as experience points toward buying a debate bonus as per the Art progression table on

title: Responding with Diatribe
heading: Responding with Diatribe
summary: A magus who studies a polemic for a season can write and circulate a diatribe whose quality is deducted from the Argument Total, gaining an Opposed to Reputation.
quotes: The diatribe quality is deducted from the current Argument Total

title: Responding with Apologia
heading: Responding with Apologia
summary: Apologia answer diatribes or the original polemic after a season of study and add their quality to the Argument Total; allies other than the original author can write them, and the writer gains a Supporter of Reputation.
quotes: the magus spends a season studying the associated work before writing either summa or tractatus in defense of the original argument

title: Taking the Debate to Tribunal
heading: Taking the Debate to Tribunal
summary: Describes how the cycle of diatribe and apologia ends in a Tribunal debate, and how bonuses and persuaded parties carry over after a win and are lost after a defeat.
quotes: Where the debate is won, indicated by a positive Argument Strength at the end of the debate, any bonus from circulating the texts also carries over to subsequent Tribunals

title: Correspondences and Other Texts
heading: Correspondences and Other Texts
summary: Debate letters between quarreling magi give a small seasonal study benefit, can serve as supporting testimony in debate, and bundling extra new items with a polemic makes it easier to circulate.
quotes: gains +1 on attempts to circulate the text

title: Winning the Argument Outline
heading: Winning the Argument Outline
summary: Step-by-step summary of the polemic procedure from defining the argument and writing the text through circulation, apologia and diatribe to the final use of the Argument Total at Tribunal.
quotes: At Tribunal the argument total is used as experience points to buy a bonus (if the total is positive) or a penalty (if the total is negative).

title: Example Polemic, Diatribe, and Apologia
heading: Example Polemic, Diatribe, and Apologia
summary: Worked example of writing, circulating and opposing a polemic, showing Quality, circulation totals and the resulting Argument Total and debate bonus.
quotes: The polemic has a Level of 4 and a Quality of 11

title: Charters
heading: Charters
summary: Explains what a charter is and how it is structured, and why magi who engage with the mundane world will increasingly record rights and obligations in charters with nobles.

title: Military Service and Wizard War
heading: Military Service and Wizard War
summary: Discusses how military service owed under charters can be met by sending men or paying scutage rather than fighting in person, and gives the core interpretation that Wizard War needs a month's notice, which each Tribunal may rule on.
quotes: notice of a lunar month must be provided before hostilities commence

title: Optional Rule: Charter Strength
heading: Optional Rule: Charter Strength
summary: Optional rule giving each side of a charter a strength score generated by notaries, which is then tested by a seasonal search for loopholes that justify breaking provisions.
quotes: Charter Strength: Intelligence + Civil and Canon Law + Stress Die
There is a default of three botch dice for this roll

title: Realm Aligned Spells and Other Techniques
heading: Realm Aligned Spells and Other Techniques
requires: Hermetic Breakthrough: realm-aligned spells
summary: Discusses ways for magi to avoid the aura penalty of the Dominion, including realm-aligned spells as a Hermetic Breakthrough and the work of Conciatta and the learned magicians.
quotes: this is a Minor Breakthrough
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.34

title: Magical Displays Earn Reputation
heading: Using Magic for Political Leverage
requires: Saga arc: Order of Hermes as the Fourth Estate
summary: After a magus has published a polemic supporting integration, giving a community or noble a sufficiently powerful device or spell earns him experience in a Proponent Reputation.
quotes: earns the magus one experience point towards his Proponent of (ideal) Reputation

title: Warping While Under Constant Magical Effects
heading: Warping While Under Constant Magical Effects
requires: Constant enchantments on people or places
summary: Tables showing how many Warping Points and what Warping Score and effects accumulate over the years for targets under constant enchantments that improve living conditions.
quotes: The second table assumes a single level 40 enchantment producing five warping points per year.

title: Appropriate Virtues and Flaws for Warped Buildings
heading: Appropriate Virtues and Flaws
requires: Warped buildings or places
summary: Suggests the kinds of Virtues, Flaws, magical Qualities and Personal Powers a building may gain when it becomes warped.
quotes: a Personal Power (an effect of Personal Range OR constant duration of up to 25 levels)

title: Can Magi Really Heal Lepers?
heading: Can Magi Really Heal Lepers?
requires: Leprosy in the saga
summary: Distinguishes Hermetic leprosy from true leprosy (a Divine curse) and notes that magic can offset the disease's living-conditions penalty by improving a colony's conditions.
quotes: imposes a –2 living conditions modifier

title: Improving Living Conditions with Magic
heading: Living Conditions
summary: Indirect magical improvement of living conditions for aging rolls, by long-term enchantments on the environment, at the cost of Warping for whatever is under the enchantments.
quotes: For every 40 levels of spells or enchantments used to improve the target living conditions, residents gain a +1 living conditions modifier.
targets under two level 20 enchantments gain two Warping Points each year
Targets under a single level 40 enchantment gain five Warping Points per year

title: Longevity Rituals for Mundanes
heading: Longevity Effects
summary: Applies the Longevity Ritual rules to people without supernatural abilities, giving the requirements and costs, and lists the drawbacks of Warping, overstaying one's welcome and loss of fertility.
quotes: the magus needs a Creo Corpus Lab Total of at least 30
the beneficiary of the Longevity Ritual gains one Warping Point per year

title: Researching Binding Magic as a Breakthrough
heading: Binding Agreements
requires: Hermetic Breakthrough research
summary: Suggests that integrating faerie or hedge powers that enforce oaths could be a Minor or Major Hermetic Breakthrough, since Hermetic magic cannot directly enforce agreements.
quotes: Researching or integrating a particular faerie power might be a Minor Breakthrough, while allowing freedom to vary the parameters and create similar spells may be a Major Breakthrough.
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.26

title: Construction: Earth Jacketed In Stone
heading: Construction: Earth Jacketed In Stone
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Introduces the method of building an artificial island by casting Creo Terram rituals that make a thick stone wall jacketing an infill of earth.

title: Outer Wall Shapes
heading: Outer Wall Shapes
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Describes the default design of the island's sea wall, how changing its height changes its diameter, and how a few extra spell levels greatly increase its area.
quotes: an extra 5 spell levels increases the area incredibly

title: Open Ended Cylinder
heading: Open Ended Cylinder
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Gives the spell levels needed to create an open-ended cylindrical wall of a given diameter, and recommends treating a conical frustum as a cylinder for calculation.
quotes: A level 30 spell creates a wall 30 paces high, 2 paces thick, and just over 3 miles in diameter.

title: Tall Empty Cylinder
heading: Tall Empty Cylinder
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Gives the spell levels for a much taller cylindrical wall suited to deeper water, with correspondingly smaller diameters.
quotes: A level 30 spell creates a wall 240 paces high, two paces thick, and just over a third of a mile in diameter.

title: Simple Spells to Create Permanent Walls
heading: Simple Spells to Create Permanent Walls
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: A set of ritual spells that create permanent stone walls of increasing volume, showing how size magnitudes scale and noting that rituals below a certain volume gain no advantage.
quotes: which is a total of 100 cubic paces of stone
Due to the quirk of Hermetic magic that makes all Rituals fourth magnitude spells or greater

title: Open Ended Rectangular Prism
heading: Open Ended Rectangular Prism
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Gives the spell levels for walls forming a rectangular island, noting that it suffers more erosion than a cylinder and that a pyramidal frustum is a better shape.
quotes: A level 30 spell creates sufficient stone to make walls 30 paces high, 2 paces wide, and a top square with 4,166 paces (2.4 miles) per side.

title: Solid Stone Cylinder
heading: Solid Stone Cylinder
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Gives the spell levels for a single monolithic stone cylinder that can be quarried into to create rooms.
quotes: A level 30 spell creates a stone cylinder 30 paces high and 206 paces in diameter.

title: Ablative Slope
heading: Ablative Slope
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Explains how a slope of mud or sand at the base of the wall protects it from wave erosion and how its spell level compares with the wall's.
quotes: the spell to create an ablative slope is three magnitudes lower than the spell that creates the wall

title: Ornamentation
heading: Ornamentation
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Wall features can be added by raising the spell level of the initial spell, or retrofitted afterwards with Rego Terram or mundane craftsmen.

title: Maximum Magnitudes Due to Complexity
heading: Maximum Magnitudes Due to Complexity
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Suggests the troupe cap the magnitudes added by complex features, after which the magus can shape his creation freely.
quotes: after adding three magnitudes for complexity, the magus can manipulate his creation into any shape he wishes, without adding extra magnitudes

title: Fortified Wall
heading: Fortified Wall
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Lists fortress features for the sea wall and whether each adds a magnitude to the spell or merely uses stone: crenellations, fire step, height, machicolations and hoardings.
quotes: Adding crenellations adds a magnitude.

title: Sea Gates and Docks
heading: Sea Gates and Docks
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: A sea gate and internal harbor wall add a single magnitude to the wall spell, with extra material needed for the harbor.
quotes: it adds 1 magnitude because it has some metal parts, but requires no added material

title: Statuary
heading: Statuary
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Statues or reliefs on the wall cost nothing if they express the caster's sigil, otherwise they add a magnitude.
quotes: If they are an artistic motif, they add a magnitude.

title: Base Metal Walls
heading: Base Metals
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Walls of copper, bronze, brass or iron alloys cost extra magnitudes to create compared with stone, and the section gives example wall sizes by spell level.
quotes: The base spell level is two magnitudes higher, while the base Individual of is 1/27th the volume.

title: Noble Metal Walls
heading: Noble Metals
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Walls of silver or gold are possible with very high-level spells but are much more difficult than base metals and attract invaders.
quotes: Walls made of valuable metals are three magnitudes more difficult to create than walls of base metals of equivalent size.

title: Unnatural Stones
heading: Unnatural Stones
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Adding a Muto requisite lets the wall have unnatural properties, with further requisites needed for effects such as burning or self-healing.
quotes: By adding a Muto requisite to the ritual used to create the wall, magi can create stone with unnatural properties.

title: Biological Substances
heading: Biological Substances
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Walls of wood or bone are equally difficult to produce by volume, but vulnerable to predators and faerie influence, and human bone is as hard as base metal.
quotes: When calculating volumes, stone, animal bone, and wood are equally difficult to produce.

title: Dirt, With a Layer of Topsoil
heading: Dirt, With a Layer of Topsoil
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Gives the soil volumes needed to fill islands of various sizes and the Creo Terram ritual levels that provide that volume.
quotes: A level 35 spell provides up to 10 billion cubic paces of soil.

title: A Basic Quote (Island Cost)
heading: A Basic Quote
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Worked example of the spells, vis and time needed to create a circular island of a given size with a standard wall and soil fill.
quotes: that requires just two spells, a level 35 and a level 40, and 15 pawns of vis

title: Clay Fill
heading: Clay
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Clay fill is as easy to create as soil and is waterproof, so the soil calculations can be used for a topsoil-over-clay fill.
quotes: Clay is as easy to create as soil.

title: Stone Fill
heading: Stone
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Stone fill is harder to create than soil, and choosing a variety of stones adds a magnitude for complexity.
quotes: Stone is three magnitudes more difficult to create than soil of the same volume.

title: Rooms and Utility Spaces
heading: Rooms and Utility Spaces
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Excavated or created underground rooms need extra magnitudes for elaborate design, using Conjuring the Mystic Tower as a reference.
quotes: adds 3 magnitudes for elaborate design

title: Road Works
heading: Road works
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Explains why paved roads are the only worthwhile road to create magically and gives a ritual that makes road networks of a stated maximum length, with extra magnitudes for complex designs.
quotes: the maximum length for this spell, which is 3.78 miles

title: Creating Houses and Other Buildings
heading: Creating Houses and Other Buildings
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Ways of making housing on the island, including shell keeps and rituals that raise many identical cottages, with each added magnitude multiplying the number produced by ten.
quotes: Every magnitude added to the spell multiplies the number of cottages produced by ten.

title: Water Works
heading: Water Works
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Covers cisterns, canals and aqueducts on the island, with rituals that create stone-lined canals for local use and for seagoing vessels, scaled by spell level.
quotes: A single horse can draw 30 tons of cargo on a barge

title: Creating Fields and Forests
heading: Creating Fields and Forests
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Herbam rituals that create forests, acorns or grassland, where each added magnitude multiplies the quantity created by ten.
quotes: Each added magnitude multiples this number of trees by 10.

title: How Many Peasants Are Needed?
heading: How Many Peasants Are Needed?
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Gives manor size, income and peasant families per manor to estimate how many manors an island of a given size can support.
quotes: A typical manor, for a landed knight, is 600 acres.
This provides 20 Mythic Pounds of income, before expenses, each year.

title: Sources of Magic Auras
heading: Auras
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Magic auras develop in four ways: through natural beauty, ancient structures, the residue of powerful rituals, and the habitation of magical creatures, which matters for an artificial island that starts without an aura.
quotes: Magic auras develop in four main ways.

title: Story Seeds for the Residue of Great Magic (Moving an Aura)
heading: Story Seeds for the Residue of Great Magic
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Moving a site of great works usually leaves its aura behind, because the spirit of place is tied to the location; overcoming this needs a Rego Vim effect or requisite, usually a ritual opposed by the Spirit of Place.
quotes: the aura is usually left behind
related: Realms of Power: Magic p.106 Genius Loci

title: Natural Beauty (Aura Tether)
heading: Natural Beauty
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Sites of great natural beauty can tether an aura; an uninhabited rock with an aura can be enclosed by the island, or a place of archetypal wind or wave action found nearby, giving only a weak tether.
quotes: Sites of great natural beauty can provide the tether for an aura.

title: Ancient Structures (Aura Tether)
heading: Ancient Structures
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Structures slowly acquire magical tethers, and can be moved to the island while retaining some of their potency.
quotes: each century adds 1 to the strength of the tether

title: The Residue of Great Magic (Aura Tether)
heading: The Residue of Great Magic
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Rituals of sufficiently high level create magical tethers, but the rituals that build the wall and fill are normally too weak to do so unless the island is vast.
quotes: Magical tethers are created by rituals of level 45 or higher.

title: The Lair of Great Magical Creatures (Aura Tether)
heading: The Lair of Great Magical Creatures
requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
summary: Places where potent spirits dwell eventually develop auras, but such creatures prefer to move into an existing aura, so this method works best after another method has made a weak aura.
quotes: Places where potent spirits dwell eventually develop auras.
